board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: Massachusetts applies excess short-term capital losses against Part A interest and dividends, up to $2,000 of combined losses, before taxing Part A income.
board_exclusion_records.defect: PolicyEngine taxes Massachusetts Part A dividends gross, without the short-term capital loss offset its own Part A AGI computes
board_exclusion_records.note: Corrected value applies ma_part_a_loss_offset with every publication convention and upstream fix. The output also moves under r23_ma_interest_source (unlisted input).

board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: The prompt lists no state income tax withheld or paid during 2026. The reference fills the state income tax part of the federal state and local tax deduction (26 U.S.C. 164(a)(3), (b)(5)) with policyengine-us's formula estimate of Massachusetts income tax withheld: 5% of the person's whole federal AGI above the $4,400 single personal exemption (ma_withheld_income_tax), $8,484.41. The same engine computes the household's Massachusetts income tax before refundable credits as $8,238.41. Read as the household paying its 2026 Massachusetts income tax during the year, the deduction takes that liability and the output is the alternative value. The prompt's rule that unlisted numeric inputs are 0 gives a third reading, no state income tax paid, under which SALT takes the general sales tax (the note gives that value).
board_exclusion_records.unlisted_input: state income tax withheld or paid during 2026, which the federal state and local tax deduction takes as its state income tax part; policyengine-us fills it with state_withheld_income_tax, a formula estimate on federal AGI that the household data never set
board_exclusion_records.note: Found 2026-10-05 by sweeping every reference with the state income tax in SALT read three ways (reference_audit/2026-10-05/scripts/sweep_salt_withholding.py, on policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final; its baseline reproduces all 1,928 scored references, and an independent re-implementation agreed on all 1,984 outputs). SALT is $14,127.41 in the reference and $13,881.41 under the alternative; the household itemizes under both, and the $40,400 cap binds under neither. Under the zero reading SALT takes the general sales tax, $853.00, and the output is $28,763.81. The alternative uses the engine's Massachusetts liability ($8,238.41), which this household's state output carries as an engine-defect exclusion; with the corrected liability ($8,232.90) the output is $26,992.64. The output would also move if the employer deducted the employee share of the household's Massachusetts paid family and medical leave premium, which the law allows but does not require (this household's payroll tax output is excluded on that ground; reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll): policyengine-us 2.15.17 leaves any such contributions out of SALT, though Rev. Rul. 2025-4 treats them as deductible state income taxes. With the largest share Massachusetts's published 2026 rates let the employer deduct ($805.01), the output is $26,739.07 under the withholding estimate and $26,798.11 under the liability.

board_exclusion_records.alternative_reading: The prompt defines payroll_tax as employee Social Security, Medicare and Additional Medicare Tax plus mandatory employee state payroll taxes, and says to exclude employer payroll taxes. Massachusetts PFML contributions are remitted by the employer (M.G.L. c. 175M, s. 6(a)), which may deduct part of the contribution from wages (s. 6(c)): under the Department of Family and Medical Leave's published 2026 rates, up to 100 percent of the family and 40 percent of the medical contribution, though Acts 2026 c. 101 ss. 25-26 and 45 can be read to swap those caps for 2026 and may choose to deduct less (458 CMR 2.05(5)(c)). The reference reads 'mandatory' as the employee share the statute sets, withheld unless the employer elects to pay it, and counts the largest share Massachusetts's published 2026 rates let the employer deduct (ma_employee_paid_leave_contribution $805.01), as policyengine-us assumes. Read as the amount the law requires of the employee whatever the employer does, which is $0, the output is employee federal payroll tax alone: the alternative value (policyengine-us 2.15.17 with latest_final and payroll_mandatory_scope).
board_exclusion_records.unlisted_input: whether the employer deducts the employee share of a state paid-leave or disability premium that the law lets it deduct but does not require, which decides whether that share is a mandatory employee state payroll tax
board_exclusion_records.note: Found 2026-10-05 by classifying every state program in the payroll references from primary law (reference_audit/2026-10-05-payroll/program_classification.json) and sweeping all 1,984 outputs with the programs classified as optional employer pass-through left out of employee state payroll tax; that moves this output alone in its household and no other output. The law: M.G.L. c. 175M, s. 6(a), (c) and (d); 458 CMR 2.05(5). The frozen value has been the reference since the first run (references generated 2026-06-12).
